uncited: Standard rendering metrics quantify the fidelity of rendered images against ground-truth targets to evaluate the quality of radiance-field optimizations.
- Rendered image tensor $\hat{I}$ of shape $[H, W, 3]$ (RGB).
- Target (ground-truth) image tensor $I$ of shape $[H, W, 3]$ (RGB).
- Both tensors must be in the same color space and range (typically $[0, 1]$ or $[0, 255]$).
For PSNR/SSIM, direct pixel access is required.
For FID/KID, feature vectors extracted from a pre-trained Inception network are required.
**Preprocessing:** Ensure $\hat{I}$ and $I$ are aligned in resolution and color space.
- **SSIM Window Size:** Typically $11 \times 11$ or $3 \times 3$ depending on implementation.
- **FID/KID Inception Model:** Inception-v3 trained on ImageNet.
PSNR is highly sensitive to scaling errors.
- **Time Complexity:** PSNR and SSIM are $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of pixels.
LPIPS and FID/KID require forward passes through deep networks, making them significantly slower ($O(N \cdot C)$ where $C$ is the cost of the network inference).
- **Memory Complexity:** PSNR/SSIM require storing only the image tensors.
FID/KID require storing feature vectors for all images in memory or streaming them to compute statistics.
Use LPIPS for perceptual quality assessment.
Standard rendering metrics have been adopted from image processing and computer vision communities.
